title: Days to Settlement for Home-Visit Service Charges — Specimen Collection Appointments
content:
## Billing calendar note

For the service charges of a collected Mobile In-Home Collection Visit of Specimen Collection Appointments, the days to settlement are counted in calendar days up to today. Where the count starts depends on how long after the collection the charges were posted. The posting date is the latest date on which a fee was assessed on the visit, as the visit's fee record shows it; the collection date is the date on the visit record on which the specimen was collected.

| Charges posted (posting date counted in calendar days after the collection date) | Days to settlement |
|---|---|
| More than 7 days after collection | Counted from the posting date to today |
| 4 to 7 days after collection | Counted from the collection date to today, less the days of posting delay beyond 3 |
| Within 3 days of collection | Counted from the collection date to today |

**Clause.** When the charges were posted more than 7 days after the collection date, the count starts on that posting date; when they were posted 4 to 7 days after collection, the count starts on the collection date and the days of posting delay beyond 3 are taken off the count; when they were posted within 3 days of collection, the count starts on the collection date.

## Cases (hypothetical dates: collection on day C, today is day C plus 20)

| Posting date | Delay | Days to settlement |
|---|---|---|
| Day C plus 2 | 2 days | 20 |
| Day C plus 3 | 3 days | 20 |
| Day C plus 4 | 4 days | 20 less 1, that is 19 |
| Day C plus 7 | 7 days | 20 less 4, that is 16 |
| Day C plus 8 | 8 days | From day C plus 8 to day C plus 20, that is 12 |

**Point of judgement.** When the visit carries fee lines assessed on different dates, the latest of those dates is the posting date.
